# T15: GTX 1650 (Turing TU117), 2026-10-20

The RTX 4090 left the machine for an ASUS Phoenix GTX 1650 OC 4 GB (TU117). Its NVENC is version 6.6 (class 0xb4b7, the
Volta generation), its NVDEC class 0xc4b0, the host classes c46f (channel) / c461 (usermode). NullMoth 2.4.3 runs it
(display, Metal 3) but its own encoders do not register on it.

## T15.01: classes from the GPU

`rm_class(rm, RM_CLS_NVENC | _NVDEC | _CHANNEL | _USERMODE)` reads `NV0080_CTRL_CMD_GPU_GET_CLASSLIST_V2` once and picks
the first class the GPU has from Ada's down to Volta's. Every encoder, decoder and tool uses it; the NVENC setup magic is
`(class << 16) | 6` (0xB4B70006 on NVENC 6.6). The setup structures are the same as on Ada.

## T15.02: HEVC encode on NVENC 6.6

Our HEVC encode faulted (MMU) on the second P picture. The fourth trace of NVIDIA's Linux driver (user-approved,
`docs/traces/gtx1650-linux`) showed:
- references are given by **DPB slot**, as for H.264: `l0[0]` = slot 1 goes in `SET_IN_REF_PIC1`. Ada takes HEVC
  references by list position; ours left REF_PIC1 unset when the reference was in slot 1, which was the fault;
- the history buffer is 768 x CTB columns x (CTB rows + 1/2) bytes (Ada: 768 x CTB columns);
- **no HEVC B pictures** (NVIDIA's own driver refuses `hevc_nvenc -bf`): enc_open turns them off on 0xb4b7.

H.264 (P and B pictures) and 4:4:4 (HEVC Rext and H.264 High 4:4:4 Predictive; a lossless round trip is byte-exact) work
unchanged.

## T15.03: decoders on NVDEC 0xc4b0

Before: HEVC conformance 166/186 and x265 28/33, VP9 vectors 26/29, VP9 4K faulting.

**HEVC, wide pictures.** 3200x1800 and 4K had wrong rows at CTB edges. Turing splits pictures wider than about 3072 into
columns and fills the filter-above and SAO-above areas by width; we sized them by height. Now by the larger dimension.

**HEVC, tiles.** Every stream with at least 3 tile columns and 3 tile rows failed (`TILES_A/B`, `DBLK_D-G_VIXS`; 3x2,
2x3 and 2x2 grids passed): decoding stopped part way with status 0 (green unwritten areas in a staircase along tile edges),
or a few pixels differed at a tile edge. Enlarging one filter area at a time (each 16x), only the SAO-left area mattered.
At 1x it ran into the BSD control area behind it; 5x5 tiles at 1080p need 2x. Now 8x (under 1 MB at 4K). Result: x265
30/33 (the rest 4:2:2 / monochrome) and conformance 178/186, **the same 8 failures as on Ada** (4:2:2, pictures over 8192,
WPP_D, TSUNEQBD, EXT_A).

**HEVC through VideoToolbox.** Comparing with Apple's software decoder showed a few frames differing at random. Against
ffmpeg ours is bit-exact on every run; Apple's software HEVC decoder varies from run to run on the last frames.

**VP9, frame size.** Turing answers status 0x10 for frames 64 pixels or less in either dimension (one superblock row or
column: 8x8 to 64x64, 200x8, 8x200; 66x66 and up are bit-exact; NVIDIA lists 128x128 as VP9's minimum). Buffers sized
for 256x256 and surfaces of 128x128 made no difference. vp9dec refuses such frames on 0xc4b0 and libnvencvt refuses
such sessions, so VideoToolbox can try another decoder.

**VP9, method 0x4c8.** Two problems had one cause.
- **Large pictures:** 2048x1088, 1280x1440, 1920x3840 and 4K faulted (no completion, error notifier 0xffff), while 4096x1024
  and 640x1440 passed. Enlarging each buffer in turn, only the one behind `SET_INTRA_TOP_BUF_OFFSET` (0x4c8) mattered.
  Filled with a marker, it received W64 x H64 / 128 bytes, 32 per superblock. The first fix (35c0218) enlarged it.
- **Segmentation maps:** `15-segkey_adpq` and `19-skip` failed. A frame that keeps the previous segmentation map
  (`segmentation_update_map` 0) decoded as if segmentation were off. The output was identical with either segment buffer,
  with both filled with any value, with 64x larger buffers, with `segmentMapTemporalUpdate` set and with `segmentEnabled`
  0. Our adapted probabilities match libvpx's on every frame (`vendor/libvpx` v1.15.2 with a dump of its frame context
  after adaptation).

The user then approved a trace of NVIDIA's Linux decoder on this card (`docs/traces/vp9dec-gtx1650-linux`, the first
decoder trace). NVIDIA's hardware decode is bit-exact on both vectors. Its setups, probabilities and segment maps match
ours except in details that turned out not to matter (stream start, timer, control bits, stale segmentation
probabilities, filter offsets). The one real difference: **NVIDIA's driver never sends 0x4c8 on Turing**, which
`clc5b0.h` does not list either. Without it both vectors are bit-exact on every frame, 4K decodes with the normal
buffers, and the 35c0218 enlargement is undone. HEVC on Turing never touches that buffer (marker test).

**AV1.** NVDEC 0xc4b0 and NVENC 6.6 have no AV1. av1dec_open needs NVDEC 0xc7b0 or 0xc9b0, and enc_open needs NVENC 0xc9b7
for AV1. Both now fail at open with a message.

## T15.04: libnvencvt on TU117

The GPU check (PCI device ID from the IORegistry) accepts TU117 (0x1f80-0x1fff) besides Ada (0x2600-0x28ff); the RM
fallback accepts NVENC 0xb4b7. Other Turing and Ampere cards keep NullMoth's encoders. On TU117 the AV1 encoder and decoder
are not registered. When enc_open turns B pictures off (HEVC on NVENC 6.6), the session follows: with 2 B pictures assumed,
HEVC files had 118 decode errors. A second session whose NVENC1 channel cannot be created moves to NVENC0, since the GTX
1650 and the RTX 4060 have one NVENC.

Checks through VideoToolbox (`vtencfile`, `vtdecode`, library injected):
- H.264 and HEVC encode in real-time, fast and quality modes, P-only and with B pictures (H.264); every file decodes
  without errors. On crowd_run / park_joy 1080p, two B pictures beat P-only at a lower rate, as on Ada; on vtencfile's
  synthetic pattern they do not.
- H.264, HEVC, HEVC Main 10, VP9 (4K 179 fps), MPEG-2 and MPEG-4 decode; ours is bit-exact against ffmpeg.

Lesson: vtencfile's last argument is an *output* (it writes the source it encoded). Pass a scratch path there and the clip
in `VT_SRC`. Two runs overwrote `~/vt-streams/natural/crowd60.nv12` and `park1080_60.nv12`; both were restored from the
dev VM's copies in `/root/natural` (SHA-256 checked).

## T15.05: decoder benchmark

`scripts/guest/bench-dec.sh` on the cached crowd_run streams (300 frames), table in benchmarks.md "GTX 1650":
- **H.264:** ours 447 fps at 1080p and 121 at 4K, NullMoth's 154 and 36: 2.9-3.3x, as on the 4090.
- **HEVC:** level, 609 / 574 at 1080p and 183 / 192 at 4K. Main 10 is level too (351 / 349, 94 / 93).
- **VP9:** 580 / 180 fps, only ours.
- **MPEG-2, MPEG-4 Part 2 and VP8:** below ffmpeg's 16-thread software decoders, as on Ada.

The card reaches about 40-65 % of the 4090's rates.

## T15.06: HEVC quality on the 1650

The user asked for the HEVC quality gap. It was measured on the 4090 (park_joy 4K, 72.7 vs x265 fast 74.1 VMAF), which is
out of the machine, so this works on the 1650's own gap (A/B with `scripts/guest/rc-ab.sh`, 300 frames, 1080p60,
6 Mbit/s CBR). The new `AB_Q` switch sets the constant-QP pair.

| | crowd_run VMAF | park_joy VMAF |
|---|---:|---:|
| ours (P only) | 55.2 @ 6.08 | 56.6 @ 6.10 |
| x265 fast | 56.9 @ 5.93 | 61.4 @ 6.00 |
| x265 fast, no B pictures | 55.0 @ 6.99 | 58.2 @ 6.67 |

The gap is B pictures, which NVENC 6.6 does not have for HEVC. Without them x265 needs 12-16 % more rate for about our VMAF.
Tried without gain:
- **NVIDIA's own p4 controls** traced on this card (`docs/traces/gtx1650-linux`): +-0.15. They were copied into our setups
  with a temporary `ENC_HEVC_CTRL_P/I` switch. Their search shapes and mode decision differ a lot from ours, yet they make
  no difference.
- **Our Ada p7 quality controls:** -0.4.
- **Two-pass:** -1.4 / +0.3.
- **3 references:** identical to 1 (the engine may not use more than one on P pictures).
- **Spatial AQ 1-3:** -0.1 to -1.1.
- **VBV of 2 s:** undershoots to 5.7-5.8 Mbit/s.
- **Constant QP with I 2 or 4 below P:** interpolated to 6.1 Mbit/s 54.3-54.6 / 56.4-56.5, so CBR's allocation already sits
  on that frontier.
- **Every second P picture as a non-reference TRAIL_N at QP +0..+4** (temporary `ENC_NRP`, the P-only version of B
  pictures): -1.2 to -5.6. The anchors then predict from two pictures back, and the cheaper non-reference pictures do not
  pay for that.

The experiment code was removed.

## T15.07: multiple references on NVENC 6.6

The reference set below was built so that extra references matter: two still images (crowd_run and park_joy frame 0)
alternate, so the picture two back is identical. A second reference should then make every picture almost free.

| references | HEVC, QP 30/32 | H.264, QP 30/32 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 65.83 Mbit/s | 75.04 Mbit/s |
| 2 | 65.83 Mbit/s | 75.21 Mbit/s |
| 3 | 65.83 Mbit/s | 75.21 Mbit/s |

The engine never uses a second reference. NVIDIA's own driver says why. The user approved a sixth session in the Linux VM
(2026-10-21), and there ffmpeg's `hevc_nvenc` and `h264_nvenc` with `-refs 2` stop with "Multiple reference frames are not
supported by the device": the driver reports `NV_ENC_CAPS_SUPPORT_MULTIPLE_REF_FRAMES` = 0 for this GPU and does not open
the encoder. TU117 encodes P pictures from one reference only, so no trace was needed. The extra references in our setups
(libnvencvt asks for 3) are simply unused. H.264 B pictures work because their second reference is in list 1.

## T15.11: picture-size limits

Each codec at and past NVIDIA's listed limits on the GTX 1650 (`encodeN`, the decoder tools; ffmpeg `testsrc2` streams).

| | works | beyond |
|---|---|---|
| H.264 encode | 4096x4096 | microcode error on every frame (no hang): libnvencvt refuses the session, VideoToolbox picks Apple's encoder |
| HEVC encode | 8192x8192 (and 8208x4320) | - |
| H.264 decode | 4096x2304 bit-exact | wider / taller than 4096: garbage without an error (libnvencvt already declines) |
| HEVC decode | 8192x8192, 8 / 10-bit | was: no completion above ~9 Mpixel (fixed, below) |
| VP9 decode | 8192x4352 bit-exact | - |
| MPEG-2 decode | 4080x4080 | 7680x4320: engine error (already declined above 4080) |
| MPEG-4 decode | 1920x1088 (8160 macroblocks) | more than 8192 macroblocks: every macroblock flagged as an error, 10-20x slower; now declined |

**HEVC above ~9 Mpixel.** 4160x2160 decoded, 4096x2304 did not (no completion). Only a larger filter buffer helped, so the
buffer was zero-filled and the last written byte of each area read back after the decode: the engine writes from the
filter-above area on, through the SAO-above and edge areas, one stretch of 0.375 bytes per pixel at 8-bit 4:2:0 (4K: 3.1 MB,
8192x4320: 13.2 MB), 0.5 at 10-bit or 8-bit 4:4:4, 0.68 at 12-bit 4:4:4. Our areas held 3.2 MB at 4K-sized pictures. hevcdec
now gives Turing at least half a byte per pixel and sample byte (twice that for 4:4:4) from the filter-above area on.
